artifacts.title: On Penalty-based Bilevel Gradient Descent Method
On Penalty Methods for Nonconvex Bilevel Optimization and First-Order Stochastic Approximation
A Fully First-Order Method for Stochastic Bilevel Optimization

public_problem: Design a target-neutral first-order bilevel optimization procedure for the supplied oracle family. Return one point for each of four fixed seeds within 4,000 oracle calls. The hidden evaluator checks lower-level validity, upper-level progress, finite outputs and seed reproducibility. You may use only the frozen pre-cutoff evidence in this capsule and the declared Python interface. Lower-level strong convexity must not be assumed.

assumptions: Upper and lower objectives are differentiable and have Lipschitz gradients on the bounded test domain.
The lower solution set is nonempty, but lower-level strong convexity is not assumed.
Only function values and first-order derivatives of the supplied instance are available.

research_context.formal_problem: Minimize a smooth upper objective F(x,y) subject to y belonging to the solution set of a smooth lower objective G(x,·). The supplied test family has a non-singleton or weakly curved lower solution geometry; the method may use first-order oracles only and is scored at a fixed oracle budget.

known_failures_and_conflicts.summary: A fixed penalty coefficient can trade lower feasibility against upper progress and may stall on weakly curved directions.

known_results.summary: Pre-cutoff penalty formulations provide fully first-order routes for several nonconvex bilevel settings.
Without lower-level strong convexity, hyper-objective stationarity can be hard or ill posed, so evaluation should include lower-level residuals rather than only a hyper-gradient.

research_context.research_question: Can a target-neutral, fully first-order penalty procedure achieve stable upper-level stationarity when the lower-level problem is smooth but not strongly convex?
